newsitem.title: DUBAI: Barge smuggling diesel out of Iraq sinks.
newsitem.headline: Barge smuggling diesel out of Iraq sinks.

text.p: A barge carrying about 600 tonnes of diesel fuel from Iraq in violation of U.N. sanctions sank in the Gulf after it declared it was in poor shape and needed to head to the nearest port, a U.S. navy spokesman said on Sunday.
Commander T. McCreary said the barge, towed by the UAE-flagged tug Zair, was intercepted and boarded on December 12 by U.S.-led multinational forces enforcing U.N. sanctions on Iraq.

"The barge was not in very good condition. It even had one empty tank open to the sea. We held it for a couple of days, but when the master said he needed to head to the closest port because of the poor condition we released it," he told Reuters.
"On December 15 the 140-foot (43-metre) barge sank after the weather had worsened overnight," he added. He said the diesel was in four tanks and it was not clear how much had spilled.
Shipping sources said a Bahrain-based salvage company was considering carrying out the salvage work.
McCreary said the multinational forces on December 16 escorted the tug, which had lost its steering, to a port in the region for violating the sanctions.
Iraq was recently allowed by the United Nations to export limited amounts of oil in an oil-for-food deal, but McCreary said smuggling of diesel continued.

"People who are violating sanctions are not risking their best equipment and most vessels we see coming out of Iraq are in generally poor condition and in many cases we had to assist and repair and keep vessels going while we divert them," he said.

He said multinational forces had intercepted three to four vessels a month and contraband worth $3 million in violation of the sanctions since August. They had also intercepted two vessels trying to enter Iraqi waters with car spare parts.

The multinational force has been checking shipping in the Gulf to enforce a U.N. trade embargo imposed on Iraq after its 1990 invasion of Kuwait. Iraq has complained to the United Nations that the patrols have violated its territorial waters.
